cause: Abrasive contact during handling, transport, or contact with tooling/fixtures.
impact: Cosmetic degradation; can compromise protective coatings and lead to corrosion over time.
solution: Isolate affected units; inspect handling equipment for sharp edges or misalignment.
prevention: Use protective padding in transport, audit fixture surfaces regularly, train handlers on proper grip points.

cause: Mechanical stress during forming, thermal shock, or material fatigue.
impact: Structural weakness; risk of propagation and complete failure under load.
solution: Reject affected units; do not attempt repair on structural cracks.
prevention: Review process parameters (cooling rate, press force); inspect raw material batch quality.

cause: Foreign particles introduced during molding, filling, or packaging due to unclean environment or equipment.
impact: Product safety risk, especially for consumables or sealed products; may indicate broader process contamination.
solution: Quarantine the batch; trace contamination source via nearby process steps.
prevention: Increase cleanroom/line cleaning frequency, add filtration at fill points, review supplier material cleanliness.

cause: Impact damage during handling, drop events, or excessive clamping force.
impact: Product is non-functional; safety hazard if sharp edges are exposed.
solution: Reject immediately; do not attempt field repair for structural breaks.
prevention: Review conveyor/drop heights, audit clamp force settings, add shock-absorbing packaging.

cause: Localized stress concentration, often from a pre-existing micro-crack or material defect.
impact: May appear cosmetic but can propagate into larger structural failure under use.
solution: Reject affected units; flag for material batch review if recurring.
prevention: Incoming material inspection, reduce stress concentrators in mold/die design.

cause: Excess mechanical force during assembly, coiling, or automated pick-and-place misalignment.
impact: May cause electrical shorts, intermittent connections, or complete circuit failure.
solution: Reject and inspect assembly tooling for calibration drift.
prevention: Regular calibration of pick-and-place equipment, softer gripper materials, wire tension control.

cause: Assembly step skipped or component not seated correctly during automated/manual assembly.
impact: Product is non-functional; safety-critical if the missing component is protective.
solution: Route to rework station for component insertion and re-test.
prevention: Add in-line presence-detection sensors, operator checklist audits, assembly step verification.

cause: Excessive stripping force during wire preparation, or sharp tooling contact.
impact: Risk of internal short circuit, safety hazard in powered applications.
solution: Reject unit; recalibrate stripping tool tolerance.
prevention: Regular tool wear inspection, use of tolerance-controlled automated strippers.

cause: Abrasion or cutting contact during handling, routing, or installation.
impact: Reduced protection against moisture/electrical contact; potential safety hazard.
solution: Reject or repair with certified insulation tape/sleeve if within spec tolerance.
prevention: Route cables away from sharp edges, use protective conduit in high-contact zones.

cause: Puncture from sharp object contact during handling or packaging.
impact: Compromises seal integrity (for capsules/sealed products) or surface protection.
solution: Reject affected units; inspect packaging line for protruding hardware.
prevention: Audit packaging line for sharp edges, use puncture-resistant transport trays.

cause: Inconsistent pigment mixing, curing temperature variation, or raw material batch variance.
impact: Cosmetic defect; may indicate underlying process drift affecting other properties.
solution: Flag batch for QC review; check colorant mixing ratios.
prevention: Tighter process control on mixing/curing parameters, incoming pigment batch testing.

cause: Print head misalignment, ink viscosity variation, or substrate surface irregularity.
impact: Cosmetic and potentially functional if print carries safety/regulatory information.
solution: Recalibrate print head; reject unreadable safety-critical prints.
prevention: Scheduled print head maintenance, ink viscosity monitoring.

cause: Surface finishing inconsistency or tooling mark left during production.
impact: Cosmetic defect; generally does not affect structural integrity.
solution: Flag for cosmetic-grade downgrade or rework if within polish tolerance.
prevention: Audit finishing tool condition and pressure settings.

cause: Multiple simultaneous defect mechanisms, often indicating a broader process or material issue rather than an isolated event.
impact: Compounded risk; treat with the highest severity of any individual contributing defect.
solution: Full unit inspection recommended; investigate whether defects share a common root cause.
prevention: Root-cause analysis across the full production step, not just the immediate defect.

cause: Component placement error during automated assembly, often from vibration, feeder misalignment, or calibration drift.
impact: May cause functional failure or downstream assembly issues.
solution: Route to rework; verify placement against reference template.
prevention: Regular feeder/placement machine calibration, vision-guided placement verification.

cause: Thread tension inconsistency, needle wear, or material misfeed during stitching.
impact: Seam integrity compromised; risk of separation under stress or during use.
solution: Reject and reinforce seam if within rework tolerance; otherwise scrap.
prevention: Scheduled needle replacement, thread tension calibration checks.
